$description: One screen, its states, and its annotations. Feature-scoped: it lives beside the spec that owns it, while the token set and the axis grid are project-scoped under visual/ at the root — a screen belongs to a feature, a design system does not. States marked derived:* were generated from the declared contract; states marked authored were not, and could not have been.

ratified.note: A ratified baseline, not a version. Superseded by the next ratification rather than incremented. Re-ratification is a human act; nothing here promotes itself.

states.name: empty
states.note: No amount entered yet. No HTTP status corresponds to this and no contract could have produced it.

states.name: loading
states.note: In flight. Distinct from cold-start: the previous rate is still on screen and dimmed rather than removed.

states.name: cold-start
states.note: In flight with nothing cached. The only state where the amount field is the sole content.

states.name: invalid-pair
states.note: Three responses, one state. The mapping is many-to-one and is a decision, not a derivation: 400, 404 and 422 differ to a client and are indistinguishable to a person who mistyped a currency code. Recorded here so the collapse is reviewable.

states.name: unauthorized
states.note: Reachable only with a revoked key, which a user cannot cause and cannot fix. Designed anyway because a state that renders nothing is how a blank screen ships.

states.name: rate-limited
states.note: Retry-After is required by the contract, so the state can name a time rather than say 'try again later'.

states.name: offline
states.note: No request was made. There is no status code for a request that never left the device, which is the clearest evidence that contract-derived states are a floor.

states.name: stale-cache
states.note: Derived from a field rather than a response — asOf is older than the freshness window. Sits between the two categories, and is the reason the source vocabulary is a string rather than a boolean.

annotations.name: Amount in {base}
annotations.note: A real field, not a styled label with a tap handler.

states.disabled: aria-disabled, never the disabled attribute — a disabled control is not focusable and cannot explain itself

annotations.note: The 44pt floor is measurable, so it is a token rather than prose.
Announced on change, not on every keystroke.
Colour is not the only channel: the badge carries text as well as {color.warning}, so it survives greyscale and forced-colors.
Skipped entirely under Reduce Motion — the value changes without the transition.
The one network call this screen makes.
Specified now so that answering the consent question is a switch rather than a retrofit. No event ships until it is answered. No PII in any payload.

accessibilityFloor.dynamicType: Layout holds at the largest accessibility content size without clipping or truncation.
accessibilityFloor.contrast: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and for any non-text element carrying meaning.
accessibilityFloor.note: Platform floors, restated here only because each one is measurable and therefore checkable.
